meta.description: Food truck ordering systems compared: pre-orders with a pickup time, kitchen capacity, weekly schedule, fees and contract length — checked on each vendor's site.

tldr.body: If your customers should order ahead on their phone and choose a pickup time, you need an ordering system, not just a POS. Look for four things: pickup times that follow your kitchen capacity; a weekly schedule for changing locations; low or no fees per order; and no long contract. Card readers and POS systems cover payment at the truck and complement an ordering system.

fit.oursBody: you operate at changing locations, want pre-orders with a pickup time, don't want your kitchen overloaded, and don't want a contract.
fit.oursNotBody: your customers should pay with PayPal or Klarna, or you want a certified POS with a TSE from one vendor.
fit.tillsBody: POS systems take payment at the truck and cover the TSE requirement. An ordering system works alongside a POS; it does not replace it.
fit.tillsBodyNamed: POS systems take payment at the truck and cover the TSE requirement. {names} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} also in the table above. An ordering system works alongside a POS; it does not replace it.
fit.marketplacesBody: Delivery platforms bring new customers but take commission on every order. Uber Eats states 14% for pickup and 30% for delivery by Uber couriers in Germany. Wolt says on its own website that it charges commission but gives no rates. We could not check Lieferando’s rates. That commission applies to regulars who pre-order with you, too.

faq.whatA: An ordering system takes orders online before customers reach the truck: they choose dishes and a pickup time, pay online or at pickup, and the order appears in your kitchen. A POS or card reader takes payment at the truck. The two complement each other.
faq.capacityQ: How does the system keep my kitchen from getting overloaded?
faq.capacityA: Customers only see pickup times your kitchen can actually make. The system works from each dish's prep time and how many you prepare at once.
faq.tseQ: Do I still need a POS with a TSE?
faq.tseA: HatchGrab is not a POS and has no TSE. How you record online orders in your POS is a question for your tax advisor.

method.prices: Prices are shown as the vendor states them, including sales tax.

preorder.label: Pre-orders with a chosen pickup time
preorder.explain: Customers order in advance and choose when they pick up.

capacity.label: Pickup times limited by kitchen capacity
capacity.explain: Customers only see pickup times the kitchen can actually make.

asap.explain: Customers can order without choosing a time and pick up as soon as it is ready.

payattruck.explain: Customers order online and pay when they pick up.

vans.label: Multiple trucks
vans.ours: extra trucks for an added monthly fee

fiscal.label: Certified POS for tax rules (TSE, EET, kassaregister…)
fiscal.explain: A POS system certified for the country's rules on recording sales.

term.explain: How long the business is locked in before it can cancel.

setup.label: Setup fee
setup.explain: A one-time charge to get started.
